whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Sharing and Visibility Architect exam for?

personas.label: Security-Focused Admins
personas.description: Administrators who design and troubleshoot complex sharing models, OWD configurations, and record access for large orgs with multiple user populations.

personas.label: Platform Architects
personas.description: Architects who need to prove deep expertise in Salesforce's layered security model as part of the Application Architect or CTA path.

personas.label: Compliance Specialists
personas.description: Professionals responsible for ensuring record-level data access meets regulatory and internal audit requirements across internal and external users.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Sharing and Visibility Architect Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Sharing and Visibility Architect exam is deceptively challenging because every question tests how multiple security layers interact. You need to evaluate OWD settings, role hierarchy, sharing rules, and Apex managed sharing together — not in isolation. Many candidates underestimate this exam because they are comfortable with individual sharing concepts but struggle when the exam combines them in a single scenario.
bullets: 60 questions in 120 minutes — questions require you to trace record access through multiple sharing layers simultaneously.
~68% passing score — about 41 correct answers needed, with many questions containing two plausible answers that differ by one sharing layer.
External sharing complexity — Community and portal user sharing models (Sharing Sets, external OWD, Guest User rules) trip up candidates who only study internal sharing.
Performance implications — the exam tests your understanding of sharing recalculation cost and how deep role hierarchies impact org performance.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book the exam when you can whiteboard the complete access evaluation order from OWD through Apex Managed Sharing, and confidently explain external sharing for Community licence types.

examFormat.heading: Sharing and Visibility Architect Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Nearly every question is scenario-based, describing a specific access requirement and asking you to select the correct combination of sharing mechanisms to achieve it.
bestWayToPass: Memorize the access evaluation order: OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, manual sharing, teams, Apex managed sharing — know exactly which layer is additive and which sets the floor.
Study external sharing deeply: Sharing Sets for Customer Community, roles and sharing rules for Customer Community Plus, and External Account Hierarchy for Partner Community are frequently tested.
Understand performance trade-offs: Know when sharing recalculation is triggered, how to defer it, and how role hierarchy depth affects query performance in large orgs.
Practice Apex Managed Sharing: Know how Share objects work, how to set the rowCause field, and when programmatic sharing is the only option for a business requirement.

certificationCard.description: This architect-level exam tests your ability to design record access models at scale, covering OWDs, role hierarchies, sharing rules, Apex managed sharing, and field-level security across internal and external users.

keyConcepts.h2: Sharing and Visibility Architect: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: OWD and the Security Baseline
blocks.body: [Organisation-Wide Defaults](/certifications/sharing-visibility-architect) set the baseline record access: Private (only owner and above in **role hierarchy**), Public Read Only (all users read, only owner writes), Public Read/Write (all users read and write), Controlled by Parent (detail records follow master). **OWD** is the minimum — it can only be opened wider by other mechanisms, never restricted further. The exam tests which OWD setting applies to a given scenario and what the downstream implications are for sharing mechanisms.

blocks.heading: Record Sharing: Role Hierarchy, Rules, and Manual Sharing
blocks.body: **Role Hierarchy** automatically grants managers access to their subordinates' records — this is implicit sharing. **Sharing Rules** extend access beyond **OWD** to specific roles, groups, or territories — either ownership-based or criteria-based. **Manual Sharing** allows record owners to grant access to specific users for individual records — not scalable. **Apex Sharing** (using Share objects) enables programmatic sharing for complex business rules. The exam tests which sharing mechanism is appropriate for each access requirement.

blocks.heading: External User Sharing: Communities and Partner Portals
blocks.body: External users follow a different sharing model. Sharing Sets grant external users (Customer Community licence) access to records related to their Account or Contact — without roles or **sharing rules**. External Account Hierarchy enables partner users to see records owned by users below them in the partner account hierarchy. Guest User sharing rules grant unauthenticated visitors access to specific records. Know the licence-to-sharing mechanism mapping: Customer Community → Sharing Sets, Customer Community Plus → Sharing Rules & Roles, Partner Community → External Account Hierarchy.

blocks.heading: Field and Object Security: Profiles vs Permission Sets
blocks.body: Object permissions (CRED: Create, Read, Edit, Delete) are set on Profiles and **Permission Sets**. **Field-Level Security** controls which fields a user can see and edit — also set on Profiles and Permission Sets. The effective permissions are the union of the profile and all assigned permission sets. View All and Modify All object permissions bypass the sharing model for that object. The exam tests layered permission evaluation and when to use Profiles vs Permission Sets for access management.

blocks.heading: Sharing Performance and Audit
blocks.body: Sharing recalculation runs automatically when **OWD** or **sharing rules** change — this can be a long-running operation for large orgs. Sharing recalculation can be deferred using the Defer Sharing Recalculation feature. The Sharing Hierarchy viewer shows which mechanisms grant access to a specific record. Shield Platform Encryption encrypts data at rest for fields configured with encryption — this interacts with sharing and **SOQL** performance. The exam tests when to use audit tools (Setup Audit Trail, Field History Tracking) and the performance implications of sharing configurations.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Sharing and Visibility Architect Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Sharing & Visibility Architect exam focuses entirely on Salesforce's record access model. Every question tests your ability to design and troubleshoot complex sharing configurations — from OWDs to Apex Managed Sharing.

blocks.heading: Access Evaluation Order
blocks.body: Understand the exact order in which access is evaluated: **OWD** → **Role Hierarchy** → **Sharing Rules** → **Manual Sharing** → Teams → **Apex** Managed Sharing → Profile/PermSet object permissions. Know which layers are additive.

blocks.heading: Criteria-Based Sharing Rules
blocks.body: Know the difference between Owner-Based and Criteria-Based **Sharing Rules**. Understand when criteria-based rules fire, their limits (300 per object), and how they interact with other sharing mechanisms.

blocks.heading: External Sharing Model
blocks.body: The external sharing model (**OWD** for portal users) is separate from the internal model. Know how to configure Sharing Sets for portal users and how Account Teams extend access to Experience Cloud contacts.

blocks.heading: Performance Considerations
blocks.body: Complex sharing configurations (large sharing rule counts, deep role hierarchies) cause sharing recalculation performance issues. Know how to use defer sharing calculation and design for recalculation efficiency.

blocks.heading: Apex Managed Sharing
blocks.body: **Apex** Managed Sharing uses Share objects (AccountShare, etc.) with a specific Cause value. Know how to grant, revoke, and maintain programmatic shares and how they persist through **OWD** changes.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the primary focus of a Sharing and Visibility Architect?
options: Designing sound, scalable solutions that meet sharing and visibility security requirements
sampleQuestions.explanation: They design solutions that meet sharing and visibility security requirements.
whyWrong: 'Only reports' undersells the role, which is about sharing/visibility security architecture, not reporting.
Email is unrelated to the Sharing and Visibility Architect's core focus.
Slack is unrelated to the Sharing and Visibility Architect's core focus.

sampleQuestions.question: Which layer determines the baseline record access in Salesforce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OWD defines the baseline access level for each object (Private, Public Read Only, etc.).
whyWrong: Sharing rules extend access beyond the baseline — they aren't themselves the baseline.
Permission sets grant additional feature/object access — they don't determine the baseline record-level access.
Profiles control broader access/settings but the specific baseline record access layer is OWD.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Sharing Rule?
options: To extend access to records based on ownership or criteria
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing rules open access to records that OWD would otherwise restrict.
whyWrong: 'To restrict access' is the opposite of a Sharing Rule's purpose, which is to extend access.
Sharing Rules don't delete records — that's an unrelated data operation.
Sharing Rules don't send emails — that's unrelated to their access-extension purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sharing mechanism is used for criteria-based sharing?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Criteria-Based Sharing Rules grant access based on record field values.
whyWrong: 'Only role hierarchy' misattributes criteria-based sharing to a different sharing mechanism.
'Only manual share' misattributes criteria-based sharing to a different, one-off sharing mechanism.
'Only OWD' misattributes criteria-based sharing to the baseline access setting, not the rule mechanism itself.

sampleQuestions.question: What does 'visibility' mean in the context of this certification?
options: What data a user can see based on sharing, OWD, and permissions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Visibility is what data a user can see, governed by sharing and permissions.
whyWrong: 'Only UI' misrepresents visibility, which is about data access determined by sharing/OWD/permissions, not interface design.
'Only reports' undersells visibility, which is a broader data-access concept beyond just reports.
'Only dashboards' undersells visibility, which is a broader data-access concept beyond just dashboards.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the role hierarchy contribute to sharing?
options: Inherited record access for users above in the hierarchy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Role hierarchy grants access to records owned by users below.
whyWrong: 'Nothing' contradicts the fact that role hierarchy has a real, defined contribution to record access.
'Only reports' undersells role hierarchy's actual contribution to inherited record access.
'Only dashboards' undersells role hierarchy's actual contribution to inherited record access.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sharing rule type uses ownership?
options: Owner-based (e.g., share with role, group, or territory)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Owner-based sharing rules grant access by role, group, or territory.
whyWrong: 'Criteria-based only' misattributes ownership-based sharing to the other sharing rule type.
'Manual only' misattributes rule-based ownership sharing to a different, one-off sharing mechanism.
'OWD only' misattributes ownership-based sharing rules to the baseline access setting, not the rule type itself.

sampleQuestions.question: What is manual sharing used for?
options: One-off or exceptional access to specific records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Manual sharing grants one-off access to specific records.
whyWrong: Manual sharing doesn't replace sharing rules — it complements them for exceptional cases.
'All access' misrepresents manual sharing, which grants specific, targeted access, not blanket access.
'No access' is the opposite of what manual sharing grants.

sampleQuestions.question: Which consideration applies when designing for large numbers of sharing rules?
options: Performance: rule count, criteria complexity, and recalculation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Many rules and complex criteria can affect performance.
whyWrong: 'No limit' contradicts the fact that sharing rule count and complexity have real performance implications.
'Only security' undersells the actual consideration, which is specifically about performance impact.
'Only OWD' misattributes the performance consideration to a different, unrelated setting.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Grant Access Using Hierarchies control?
options: Whether users above in role hierarchy can access subordinates' records
sampleQuestions.explanation: This setting controls role hierarchy-based record access.
whyWrong: 'Only profiles' misattributes this hierarchy access setting to a different access-control feature.
'Only OWD' misattributes this hierarchy-specific setting to the baseline access configuration.
'Only permission sets' misattributes this hierarchy-specific setting to a different access-control feature.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object supports Territory Management sharing?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Territory and Territory Model enable territory-based sharing.
whyWrong: Account alone doesn't support the territory-specific sharing structure being asked about.
Opportunity alone doesn't itself define the territory model — that's a separate structure.
Lead alone doesn't support Territory Management's sharing structure.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Permission Set Group?
options: To bundle permission sets and simplify assignment
sampleQuestions.explanation: Permission Set Groups bundle permission sets for easier assignment.
whyWrong: Permission Set Groups don't replace profiles — every user still needs one profile.
Permission Set Groups don't replace sharing rules — those are a separate record-access mechanism.
Permission Set Groups don't create OWD settings — that's a separate baseline configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: Which data access pattern can impact performance?
options: Sharing rule recalculation, report filters, and list view limits
sampleQuestions.explanation: Recalculation, report filters, and limits affect performance.
whyWrong: 'No impact' contradicts the fact that sharing rule recalculation genuinely affects performance.
'Only OWD' undersells the broader set of access patterns (sharing recalculation, report filters, list views) that impact performance.
'Only manual share' undersells the broader set of access patterns that impact performance.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Public Read Only OWD mean?
options: All users can read all records; only owners can edit
sampleQuestions.explanation: Public Read Only allows read for all; only owners can edit.
whyWrong: 'No access' is the opposite of what Public Read Only grants.
'All can edit' misrepresents Public Read Only, which specifically restricts editing to owners.
'Private' is the opposite, most restrictive OWD setting, not what Public Read Only means.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice supports maintainable sharing design?
options: Minimize rules, use criteria wisely, and document design
sampleQuestions.explanation: Fewer rules, clear criteria, and documentation support maintainability.
whyWrong: 'Unlimited rules' contradicts the best practice of minimizing rule count for maintainability.
'Manual share only' undersells the broader best practice, which includes rule design and documentation.
'No documentation' contradicts the fact that documenting design is a core best practice.
